details: Moved the shared Requests, Connections, DNS and Logs search field from the top toolbar to a persistent Flutter-style bottom capsule.
Each tab retains its own query and keyword chips across tab switches, primary navigation and Activity recreation.
The inline clear button clears text while retaining focus; the adjacent cancel action clears text, hides the IME and leaves the docked field visible.
List content reserves space for the search dock; the search dock and snackbar are raised above the main navigation dock when glass overlap is enabled.
change.singlePageEntrypoints: Standalone Requests, DNS and Logs pages keep their existing toolbar search.

deviceTests.checks: All four MainActivity tabs keep separate queries; cancel empties EditableText and retains the dock.
Selected tab and search text restore across primary navigation and Activity recreation.
The four observation tabs expose the docked search and retain the tools return path.
All four query filters work on the complete fixture lists and remain isolated by tab.

observed: The dock sits above the main navigation dock without overlap.
The dock moves above the visible soft keyboard while typing.
Query results replace the prior content; cancel closes the keyboard, clears the query and keeps the empty dock visible.
visualInspection.glass: Disabled/default state retained; only the inset path is provided for the glass-enabled layout.

perfettoDiscardProbes.interpretation: Three separately configured captures retained the same global discarded count while their data source sets differed; this supports a service/producer-snapshot scope rather than loss in each trace buffer, but is not enough to prove the counter owner or reset lifetime. The earlier real DropdownMenu trace had 2 FrameTimeline rows and fence lifecycle events but no wait-start/end; it cannot attribute a menu frame or establish a performance gain.

limits: The probe series did not restart Perfetto service and did not isolate an identified producer; the global discarded source remains open.
The menu trace was a Debug build and had too few app-surface frames for menu close or RenderThread attribution.
Other subpages and a non-empty live connection/connection-details comparison remain outstanding.
No stable performance improvement is claimed; glass remains disabled by default.
